newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah settles but still volatile.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah settles but still volatile.

text.p: Election concerns kept the Indonesian rupiah volatile on Friday, but it stabilised in late trading after hitting an all-time low of 2,440.5, dealers said.

Dealers said the rupiah continued its downtrend on Friday after it tumbled about 15 points on Thursday before recovering slightly as operators tried to factor in possible disturbances in the election campaign that starts on Sunday.
But they said the currency stabilised in Friday afternoon trading, with spot rupiah at 2,436.70/37.5 at 0900 GMT. It opened at 2,432/33.

Dealers said options-related and stop-loss rupiah selling had triggered the sharp fall over the past two days, but the rupiah was expected to firm up gradually if there was a quiet start to the election campaign. The ruling Golkar is expected to win comfortably in the May 29 polls.
"The rupiah has settled down for now. But I think the focus is now on Sunday. People are just covering short positions. I think it's normal at this stage," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,436.0/37.0 and 2,436.5/37.0, respectively.
Dealers said a relatively ample rupiah market had helped operators buy dollars in the past two days. Overnight rupiah fell to 7.5 percent from 12.0 percent in the morning.
Overnight swap was at 0.9/1.0 and tom.next at 0.40/0.43.
Winston Koh of JP Morgan said the rupiah weakness was a reflection of the concerns people had going into the election.
"It's pretty much within expectations. People don't want to be long in the rupiah over this period," Koh said.
But Koh and other economists were generally confident the rupiah would recover after the elections.

"Post-election we should see the rupiah trading stronger relative to the band, possibly trading toward the bottom once again," Koh said, adding that most people were comfortable with the long-term view of the rupiah.
One Japanese bank dealer said he expected the rupiah to recover gradually next week if nothing major happened at the outset of the campaign.
"The crucial point is Sunday and Monday. People are looking at the start of the campaign which should give indications whether the authorities have things under control," another dealer said.
Dealers said the rupiah weakness was not really a concern yet because it was still far below the mid-rate of the band.
Dealers said swap rates were seen edging up slightly on covering, especially in tom/next swaps, reflected by relatively expensive rates despite an ample rupiah market.
One economist said swap rates had increased, but the swap market was not fully driven in, suggesting the turbulence in the spot market was driven by speculation than by fundamentals.
One-month swap was at 12.0/12.5, two at 25.5/27.0, three at 37.00/37.25 and six at 74.5/75.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,404/2,596 and the conversion band at 2,404/2,452 on Friday.
